explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates GPT-4-based metric against human annotations by comparing error counts at word, example, and domain levels using Pearson correlation coefficients

prompts.notes: Prompt format described but exact wording not fully reproduced; description includes requirements for JSON output format and error categorization

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: weak agreement on word level, stronger on example level (0.53) and domain level (0.85)

guidelines.notes: Provided error taxonomy descriptions and annotation interface details; full instructions in Appendix B with examples

sample_size.notes: Full test set evaluated by both methods; additional dual-annotation subset of 100 examples for human agreement analysis

correlation_interpretation.interpretation: weak to strong depending on granularity
correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Not explicitly defined, but progression from weak (0.26) to strong (0.93) is noted

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 shows weak agreement with humans at word level (r=0.26), moderate at example level (r=0.52), and strong at domain level (r=0.93), with agreement patterns similar to human inter-annotator agreement.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate the same four error categories with identical instructions and format
